description: A season is composed of the races held in that year; a race cannot exist without belonging to a championship season.

connection_condition: results.raceId identifies the race each entry belongs to
description: A race classification is composed of its entry records; a result row has no meaning apart from the race it belongs to.
A driver appears in race result entries; the same driver can occupy more than one entry in a single race where a car was shared, so the link is not one-to-one.
A constructor fields the cars recorded in race result entries.
A race is hosted at a circuit; the circuit is a venue rather than a whole composed of races, so this is a business association reinforced by a foreign key.

connection_condition: results and qualifying rows pair driverId with constructorId within the same race
description: A driver competes for a constructor, but the pairing is not stable for a whole season or career.
A race win is derived from the finishing position: it holds exactly when the finishing position equals 1.
A podium finish is derived from the finishing order: it holds when the entry is among the first three by finishing order.
A race win is a specific case of a podium finish; the set of wins is a subset of the set of podium finishes.
The race fastest lap of an entry is derived as the minimum lap time recorded by that entry in the race.
Total race time is derived from the lap times accumulated over the race distance together with pit-lane time, so the two concepts are consistent in magnitude for a full race distance.
Season-to-date championship points are derived by accumulating race points within a season under era-specific rules about which results count.
Championship position is derived by ranking competitors on their season-to-date championship points.

connection_condition: results rows aggregated by race and constructor, and constructorResults rows, key the same race and constructor combination
description: Both concepts express championship points awarded for one race, recorded once per driver entry and once per constructor entry; they agree except where era rules counted only one car per constructor.
A retirement is a specific outcome of a race entry; retirement entries form a subset of all result entries.
A classified finisher is a specific outcome of a race entry; classified entries form a subset of all result entries.

The classification code is derived from the car status together with the classification rules: a non-finish status becomes R, disqualification becomes D, exclusion becomes E, withdrawal becomes W and failure to qualify becomes F.
Every race entry carries exactly one car status describing its outcome or failure reason.
A driver carries one nationality value used for demographic analysis.
A constructor carries one nationality value drawn from a vocabulary that only partly overlaps the driver vocabulary.

connection_condition: circuits.country holds the host country of the circuit
description: A circuit is located in one country; the country vocabulary is nominal and shares no values with the adjectival nationality vocabulary.

connection_condition: more than one row shares a race and driver, or more than two distinct drivers share a race and constructor
description: Shared drives make the result entry, rather than the race and driver pair, the atomic unit of participation in the affected era.

connection_condition: results.grid and qualifying.position describe the same race weekend but diverge when penalties or pit-lane starts apply
description: Grid slot and qualifying classification usually agree but are distinct concepts; grid slots of 0 correspond to entries without a qualifying classification.

connection_condition: results.number and qualifying.number carry the number used in a race, while drivers.number holds a permanent number only from 2014
description: Car numbers identify entries within a race but are not a stable driver identifier across seasons.
